key_insight: Multiwavelength excitation photoluminescence can non-destructively separate interface-driven from bulk-driven degradation, revealing that PEABF4 initially passivates the ETL/perovskite interface but later accelerates depth-spreading recombination losses under heat.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical diagnostic for tuning interfacial treatments and identifying where stability failures originate in perovskite solar cells during thermal aging.
method: Multiwavelength excitation PL maps depth-sensitive recombination changes without destructive sectioning.
Compare PL decay versus excitation wavelength to distinguish interface-dominated and bulk-dominated losses.
Use diffusion-recombination simulations to link PL signatures to surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime changes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that PEABF4 reduces interfacial recombination initially, but after thermal aging the PL signatures broaden from the ETL/perovskite interface into the absorber, consistent with simulation-based interpretation.
watch_item: PL-based depth interpretation depends on accurate modeling and optical absorption assumptions, so wavelength-dependent signals should be validated carefully against complementary degradation measurements.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
